Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of UPT established by the Regional Government that functions as an information center, service center and empowerment center for women and children. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives including among others grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including among others domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 4

Letter a Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/grabbing, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.

Letter b Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will Letter c Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with other persons for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/ord. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/orc. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter f Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/orb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 7

The responsibility of the community as referred to in Article 5 letter b is implemented in the form of: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; and
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties.

Point f Critical education for women victims of violence is an effort to build women's awareness of their rights.

The purpose of implementing critical education is to help decision-making and prevent becoming a victim of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for women victims of violence consist of: training on gender equality and justice, education on reproductive health for women, and providing understanding of laws and regulations in the field of protection of women and children.

Point a Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience within the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members.

Point b Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence that occur in their environment.

Point c Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, strive to eliminate provisions that do not side with victims of violence.

Point d Sufficiently clear Sufficiently clear Point a Complaint, consultation, and counseling services include: a. identification or initial recording of victims; and
b. informed consent, namely medical action consent given by the victim or their closest family after receiving a complete explanation regarding the medical action to be performed on the victim.

Point b Accompaniment services include:
a. accompanying victims during the examination and health recovery process;
b. accompanying victims during the medicolegal process, namely medical services to provide optimal professional assistance in utilizing medical science for the purposes of law enforcement and justice. Medicolegal services include, among others: visum et repertum and visum et psychiatricum;
c. accompanying victims during the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court;
d. monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court; e. maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including coverage by mass media;
f. coordinating with other companions; and g. providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.

Point c Health services include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and c. referral to health services.

Point d Social rehabilitation services are services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

Forms of social rehabilitation services through the provision of safe houses and social support.

Social support is carried out through:
a. spiritual guidance to victims; and b. psychological recovery of victims.

Safe House (Shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. Point e Legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and court hearing examination levels and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Point f Social reintegration services aim to return victims to their families and social environment.

Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. District/City Governments within one Regional area of East Java Province;
b. related government and non-government agencies and institutions; and c. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Point g Economic independence services through providing economic access are given to victims of violence, especially women victims of violence so they can be independent in running and maintaining their lives. Such economic services can be carried out by providing training that is appropriate to the skills or talents possessed by victims, so that victims can develop the skills or talents they possess when victims return to community life. In addition, PPT can provide business information and job vacancies related to the skills or abilities possessed by victims of violence.

CHAPTER III

RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 5 The implementation of protection for victims of violence is the joint responsibility of:

a. regional government;

b. community;

c. family; and

d. parents.

Article 17

The Regional Government, UPT and the community are obliged to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence. The form of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence (2) as referred to in paragraph (1) is the fulfillment of the basic rights of children according to their needs.

CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING AND REPORTING

Article 23

1. Monitoring of the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out periodically and in an integrated manner every 6 (six) months by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Reporting on the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out 1 (one) time per year and is coordinated by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 22 (1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.

2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of:

a. forming family partners at the village/sub-district level; b. forming women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 24

1. Funding for the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is sourced from: a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. other sources of funds that are not binding based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Budget management for the implementation of protection of victims of violence is carried out with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 18

The implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence is realized among others through the establishment of an integrated, one-stop and networked UPT established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions or other institutions.

The UPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is P2TP2A (2) or similar institutions that have the same functions and roles.

Letter a What is meant by "respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims" is the guarantee of fulfillment of the basic rights of victims.

Letter b What is meant by "justice" and gender equality is a condition where women are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Regional Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so that the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/orb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

13. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of UPT established by the Regional Government that functions as an information center, service center and empowerment center for women and children. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives including among others grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including among others domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 4

Letter a Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/grabbing, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.

Letter b Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will Letter c Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with other persons for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/ord. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/orc. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter f Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/orb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 4

Letter a Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/grabbing, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.

Letter b Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will Letter c Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with other persons for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/ord. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/orc. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter f Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/orb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and court hearing examination levels and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Point f Social reintegration services aim to return victims to their families and social environment.

Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. District/City Governments within one Regional area of East Java Province;
b. related government and non-government agencies and institutions; and c. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Point g Economic independence services through providing economic access are given to victims of violence, especially women victims of violence so they can be independent in running and maintaining their lives. Such economic services can be carried out by providing training that is appropriate to the skills or talents possessed by victims, so that victims can develop the skills or talents they possess when victims return to community life. In addition, PPT can provide business information and job vacancies related to the skills or abilities possessed by victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of UPT established by the Regional Government that functions as an information center, service center and empowerment center for women and children. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives including among others grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including among others domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

Letter a Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/grabbing, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.

Letter b Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will Letter c Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with other persons for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/ord. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/orc. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter f Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/orb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING AND REPORTING

Article 23

1. Monitoring of the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out periodically and in an integrated manner every 6 (six) months by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Reporting on the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out 1 (one) time per year and is coordinated by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Point f Social reintegration services aim to return victims to their families and social environment.

Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. District/City Governments within one Regional area of East Java Province;
b. related government and non-government agencies and institutions; and c. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Point g Economic independence services through providing economic access are given to victims of violence, especially women victims of violence so they can be independent in running and maintaining their lives. Such economic services can be carried out by providing training that is appropriate to the skills or talents possessed by victims, so that victims can develop the skills or talents they possess when victims return to community life. I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

d. monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court; e. maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including coverage by mass media;
f. coordinating with other companions; and g. providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.

Point c Health services include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and c. referral to health services.

Point d Social rehabilitation services are services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

Forms of social rehabilitation services through the provision of safe houses and social support.

Social support is carried out through:
a. spiritual guidance to victims; and b. psychological recovery of victims.

Safe House (Shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. Point e Legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and court hearing examination levels and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Point f Social reintegration services aim to return victims to their families and social environment.

Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. District/City Governments within one Regional area of East Java Province;
b. related government and non-government agencies and institutions; and c. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Point g Economic independence services through providing economic access are given to victims of violence, especially women victims of violence so they can be independent in running and maintaining their lives. Such economic services can be carried out by providing training that is appropriate to the skills or talents possessed by victims, so that victims can develop the skills or talents they possess when victims return to community life. In addition, PPT can provide business information and job vacancies related to the skills or abilities possessed by victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of UPT established by the Regional Government that functions as an information center, service center and empowerment center for women and children. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives including among others grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including among others domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.

Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.

Article 4

Letter a Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/grabbing, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.

Letter b Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will Letter c Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with other persons for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/ord. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/orc. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter f Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/orb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 8

Family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).

Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

2. Reporting on the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out 1 (one) time per year and is coordinated by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 5 The implementation of protection for victims of violence is the joint responsibility of:
